title: Establish interaction contracts for dense switches and inline number fields
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background: During the compact-density audit we observed inconsistent micro-interaction timing, hit targets, and validation recovery for dense toggles (switches) and inline numeric inputs used in tables and bulk-edit flows. These inconsistencies produce a brittle keyboard experience and visual 'jank' on error recovery across Console and form-heavy surfaces.

Goal: Define a small, opinionated interaction contract (timing tokens, focus rules, validation persistence, and network-commit behavior) for two component families: dense switch (compact toggle) and inline-number (stepper / small numeric text field). Deliver a token set, annotated component variants in Figma, and a short dev spec that engineers can implement with an opt-in sync flag for server commit.

Proposed solution:
- Motion & timing tokens: introduce --motion-interaction-fast (60ms), --motion-interaction-medium (160ms), --motion-debounce-inline-commit (250ms), and --motion-error-assertive (200ms shake).
- Focus & hit targets: require 32px minimum hit area for switches on touch, maintain 24px visual density but increase invisible hit target via padding. Keyboard focus visible ring unchanged but appearing with --motion-interaction-fast delay to avoid flash on pointer interactions.
- Validation & recovery: error states are persistent until corrected (do not auto-dismiss). Inline-number fields show immediate local validation (format/min/max) and queue a debounced server commit (250ms) for non-blocking UX; server errors surface in ARIA-live region and keep the input focused for recovery.
- API contract: add an optional data-attribute/data-prop `data-commit-mode="debounced"|"sync"` so pages that must guarantee immediate persistence (bulk edits with transactional semantics) can opt into synchronous commits.
- Accessibility: ensure each inline-number change announces via aria-live when server commit results in an error; switches should expose aria-checked and have clear labels when used in dense table rows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Immediate commit avoids divergence between client/server state but increases server load and latency; debounced commit favors responsiveness and batching. Engineering requested an opt-in approach to satisfy both use-cases.
- Increasing hit targets can slightly change compact visual layout; we prefer invisible padding to preserve visual density while improving touch/keyboard success rates.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before moving to Done):
1) Figma artifacts for both components with annotated motion tokens and hit-area guidance.
2) Motion tokens pushed to design token repo and a short migration note for devs.
3) Dev spec that includes `data-commit-mode` examples, ARIA patterns, and unit test suggestions.
4) Cross-team review sign-off from Eng (ENG-4620) and PM (PM-980).

Deliverables:
- Figma: dense-switch + inline-number frames with token map (link in comments).
- Token PR: design-tokens/motion-dense.json with the new tokens.
- Implementation guidance doc: docs.redwood.ai/design/dense-interactions (link in comments).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Engineering complexity integrating debounce with KV cache. Mitigation: small spike (ENG-4620) to prototype behavior with existing runtime cache patterns.
- Risk: Accessibility regressions if ARIA announcements are not precise. Mitigation: include a11y test checklist and pair-review with accessibility engineer during implementation.
comments: 2025-11-13 Priya Kapoor: Created ticket after discovery during compact-density pass. Observed inconsistent toggle hit targets and recovery states for numeric stepper fields when validation errors occur.

2025-11-20 Liam O'Connor: Ran quick usability tests with 6 engineers; average recovery time from error was 2.8s and users reported 'jumpy' focus behavior. Proposed threshold timing changes for focus transitions: 80-120ms for hover->focus, 160-200ms for error shake animation.

2025-12-04 Design crit: Agreed on 3 interaction contracts: 1) Non-destructive toggle flip should be instant with 60ms feedback, 2) inline numeric increment should debounce input commit to backend at 250ms, but local validation immediate, 3) error state must persist until correction rather than auto-dismiss. Action: produce tokens for motion and a small component variant spec.

2025-12-18 Liam O'Connor: Uploaded Figma frames for 'dense-switch' and 'inline-number' variants. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/design-system/dense-interactions. Link to draft spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/dense-switches-inline-number.md

2025-12-22 PM feedback (Aisha Malik): Ensure compatibility with Console table rows where inline number fields are used in bulk-edit mode. PM requests include keyboard-first recoverability and ARIA live region updates.

2025-12-29 ENG review (Diego Ramos): Raised concern about debounce vs KV cache sync with runtime. Engineering suggests an API opt-in flag to align client-side debounce with server commit to avoid double-applies. Assigned ENG-4620 as dependency.
2026-01-04 Liam O'Connor: Updated acceptance criteria and UI tokens; ready for cross-team review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/514
